result.rationale:
The diff confirms the mechanism: TopicEmbed.import only validates `url =~ /^https?\:///` and then interpolates the raw url into HTML: `contents << "
#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")} "`. Posts created use cook_method raw_html (cook returns raw directly) and the embed view renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so unescaped URL characters (quotes, angle brackets) in feed-controlled i.link/i.id or disqus link values yield stored XSS. No escaping or sanitization of the url appears anywhere in the diff.

judged_text: import interpolates the unescaped url into both the href attribute and the link text of the 'Imported from' footer, and the only validation is the `^https?://` prefix regex, so a url like `http://x/<script>alert(1)</script>` or `http://x/' onmouseover='alert(1)` passes and is stored as live HTML. Feed-controlled link values (i.link / i.id in poll_feed) and disqus export links inject script tags and event-handler attributes into imported posts, giving stored XSS wherever cooked is rendered raw — the PR's stated 'URL validation' objective checks the scheme but not the characters that matter for HTML injection.
